So exp75's gate (K2 counts) would false-FAIL exp76a on edges and forks, and the expected exp76a is exp75's nodes plus exp70b's edges (238,328 data rows). In the exp76a notebook, coordinject (cell 8) runs after the pipeline cell that applies FORKMID and writes the CSV (cell 7). It rewrites only z/y/x, checks the line count and is fail-soft ('COORDINJECT FAILED', CSV unchanged). So the edges cannot differ from exp70b's, and the 'sha != ed7101bf' check catches a silent fail-soft. On the clean exp75 and exp70b logs the keyword items do not false-fire: Traceback/FAILED/SKIPPED/DEADLINE:/FALLING BACK = 0; LOWREFINE is 8 raw lines, 4 distinct each printed twice; DIVINS ENABLED = 1; FORKMID = 1 in exp70b. Rules and schedule: this is a gate, not a new mechanism. R8 does not bind the aggressive-mode public rungs (CONTEXT 12:01Z/12:12Z), coordinject files are PUBLIC-ONLY (16:08Z (2)), and the stage is off by default and fail-soft. Kaggle status at 18:14Z: exp76a still QUEUED (pushed 16:33Z; exp75 waited about 4 h), so the 23:45Z fallback (exp76a -> exp72 -> exp75) can still be reached. Small gaps, not refutations: (a) '99.9% identical' does not say which columns; (b) nothing checks that the 10.5 h deadline is anchored at kernel start or that the workers ran on CUDA; (c) there is no runtime item; (d) 'COORDINJECT_WORKER SKIP (deadline)' does not match 'SKIPPED' (the videos=4/4 item covers it).
fix: Adopt the gate with these sharpened items, still logged as one PASS/FAIL line. exp76a is GO iff all of these hold: (1) validate_csv ok; 238,328 data rows; sha256 != ed7101bf and != d6d9d808. (2) Edge rows (all columns, id included) == exp70b's: 117,076 edges, 74 forks. Record the count of differing rows. (4) 0 duplicate (dataset,t,z,y,x). (5) 'COORDINJECT SUMMARY: videos=4/4' with replaced 0.90-0.93 (exp75 0.915). The 'COORDINJECT:' line shows 2 workers on 2 GPUs and kernel elapsed > 0 (exp75: 1809 s, which shows KERNEL_START_TS anchors the 37800 s deadline). Both worker start lines show device=cuda.
